<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches prebuilt binaries from the official GitHub repository of the project (https://github.com/nao1215/jsonize) for both x86_64 and aarch64 architectures. The source URLs point to release artifacts, which are standard practices for binary packages. Checksums are provided inline in the PKGBUILD and verified via a `sha256sum -c` check using a processed version of the upstream checksums.txt file. The `verify()` function adjusts filenames in the checksum file to match the local downloaded names, which is a common technique when upstream checksums refer to differently named files.

The build process does not involve any dynamic downloading or execution of code beyond what is declared in the source array. It installs only the binary, license, and documentation files into appropriate system directories. There are no uses of dangerous patterns such as `eval`, `curl | bash`, or obfuscated commands. All operations align with standard AUR packaging practices for a `-bin` package.

Although the pkgver is fixed and not automatically updated (e.g., via git tags), this is not inherently unsafe—just a maintenance choice by the packager. The use of fixed, pinned checksums for each architecture-specific download ensures integrity. No network requests, file modifications, or executions occur outside the expected scope of building and installing the package.
</details>

It declares the package base, version, architecture support, license, source URLs, and checksums. All sources point to the official GitHub repository of the project (https://github.com/nao1215/jsonize), specifically to tagged release assets, which is a standard and expected practice.

The sources include a checksum file and two precompiled binaries (one for x86_64 and one for aarch64), each with corresponding `sha256sums` provided inline. These checksums allow `makepkg` to verify the integrity of the downloaded binaries, ensuring they have not been tampered with in transit. There are no network operations, scripts, or executable commands in this file, as it is purely declarative.

No obfuscation, suspicious URLs, or unauthorized system modifications are present. The use of prebuilt binaries (`jsonize-bin`) is common for Rust or Go tools where users prefer not to compile from source. The package conflicts with `jsonize` and provides `jz`, which are normal packaging conventions. Overall, this file adheres to standard AUR packaging practices and presents no evidence of malicious behavior.
</details>
